1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Doldari village for three days. Kim Haneul’s older sister had left for Seoul in the spring, and since then Haneul had been running the village’s little apothecary on her own.
As the day grew dark, she closed the shutters, counted the money she had earned that day, put out the lamp, and went upstairs.
Just as she lay down, a frantic knocking came from downstairs, followed by a man’s voice: “Is anyone there?”
At the door stood a young man soaked to the skin. The cloth wrapped around his left arm was soaked with blood. He introduced himself as Park Junho and said he was from the Azure Dragon Society.
“Please treat my wound,” Park Junho said in a low voice. “I’ll pay you. Will three thousand five hundred nyang be enough?”
He took a letter wrapped in oiled paper from his coat. “I must deliver this letter to Cheongpungsa by the eighteenth of May.”
Haneul thought to herself. The neighbors were already jealous that the apothecary was doing well, and now a strange man had shown up in the middle of the night.
Still, Haneul did not accept the money and only said, “I’ll take you to the mountain early tomorrow morning.”
2: As soon as day broke, the two set out. Haneul carried a basket on her back, and inside it were rice balls, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain they met old Lee Youngsoo, who was splitting firewood. The old man set down his axe and lowered his voice. The previous evening, three strangers had been at the edge of the village asking about an injured young man.
"Haneul, take the side path," Lee Youngsoo said. "The main road is dangerous." Haneul thanked the old man.
The side path was narrow and slippery. Haneul led the way, planting each step firmly. Park Junho followed behind in silence.

By noon the rain had stopped and the mountain mist was slowly lifting, and the roof of Cheongpungsa began to appear in the distance. A nun stood in front of the temple gate. It was Jeonghye, the nun who received guests at the temple.
Jeonghye took the letter, checked the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting two whole years for this letter."
Park Junho said to Haneul, "You saved my life." Haneul smiled and replied, "Then next time you come, fix the roof of the medicine shop or something." Park Junho stayed at the temple.
Toward evening, Haneul came down the mountain alone. By the time she got home, it was already dark. She lit the oil lamp and sat behind the counter for a long while.
